description: [Review finding] Representative-scale DocumentCache qualification is not actually evidenced. The DMS-1317 story requires qualifying interrupted baseline/rebuild restart from the beginning at representative scale against predefined completion-time, database-load, and repeated queue-DML/write-amplification limits, and requires creating a durable-baseline-cursor Jira ticket if a limit fails. The branch currently defines thresholds and result artifact expectations in `reference/document-cache/performance-qualification.md`, but `eng/performance/invoke-documentcache-qualification.ps1` only runs bounded unit/query-plan guards and optional explicit writer evidence, then writes a summary listing required follow-up artifacts. No checked-in measured qualification artifacts such as `threshold-results.json`, outage drain evidence, or provider metrics are present. Simplest responsible solution: add validation for a committed `threshold-results.json` plus required evidence artifact paths, then add the representative-run result artifacts for PostgreSQL and SQL Server. DMS-1317 should not be marked complete without those measured results.
acceptance-criteria: `eng/performance/invoke-documentcache-qualification.ps1` validates the committed representative-run `threshold-results.json` against the provider threshold rows documented in `reference/document-cache/performance-qualification.md`.

The validation checks that every required result artifact path exists, including `qualification-summary.md`, `threshold-results.json`, query-plan guard output, outage-drain evidence, PostgreSQL WAL/vacuum/bloat evidence, and SQL Server log/ghost/index evidence.

The representative-run artifacts include measured PostgreSQL and SQL Server results for baseline/rebuild completion time, interrupted restart-from-beginning completion time, database CPU/IO/log pressure, repeated queue DML or write amplification, status/oldest-work latency, canonical write overhead, queue growth and drain after outage, and same-document enqueue/ack lock waits.
`threshold-results.json` records one row per provider threshold with measured value, pass/fail, evidence path, and reviewer note.

If any interrupted baseline/rebuild restart-from-beginning limit fails, the results record the durable-baseline-cursor Jira ticket and the branch does not claim production qualification without that prerequisite.

`reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md`, `reference/document-cache/performance-qualification.md`, and this task list no longer imply that DMS-1317 representative-scale qualification is complete based only on threshold documentation or bounded CI guards.
steps-to-verify: Run the new qualification validation mode against the committed representative-run artifact directory.
Manually confirm the PostgreSQL and SQL Server measured-result rows match the thresholds in `reference/document-cache/performance-qualification.md` and that every evidence path resolves.

description: [Review finding] The completed-projection update tests can pass through read-time direct fill instead of proving the background projector update path. Both provider wrappers enable read acceleration and set `DocumentCacheReadAccelerationDirectFillTimeout` to `00:00:05`. The shared scenario performs a stale-cache GET before `DrainProjectionUntilIdleAsync`, and the read coordinator direct-fills stale rows by materializing and writing through `DocumentCacheWriterPurpose.DirectFill`. The later assertion explicitly allows "projection or direct fill" to acknowledge the update work row, so a broken ordinary projector update path could still pass. Simplest responsible solution: move the stale-cache GET until after `DrainProjectionUntilIdleAsync` in the completed-projection scenario, so the test proves the background projector updated and acknowledged the work row before any read can direct-fill it.
acceptance-criteria: In the ordinary-resource completed-projection scenario, after API PUT the test asserts the work row exists and the cache row is stale, then calls `DrainProjectionUntilIdleAsync` before any GET-by-id or query path that can trigger direct fill.

In the descriptor completed-projection scenario, after descriptor API update the test asserts the work row exists and the cache row is stale, then calls `DrainProjectionUntilIdleAsync` before any GET-by-id or query path that can trigger direct fill.

After the drain, the tests assert the work row is gone because projection acknowledged it, the cache row contains the updated content version, stream etag, and JSON, and subsequent reads return the updated representation from the cache path.
The completed-projection scenario no longer uses assertion text that allows "projection or direct fill" for the projector acknowledgement check.
The completed-projection scenario does not contain a pre-drain stale-cache GET or query that can repair the cache and remove work through direct fill before the projector assertion is made.
steps-to-verify: Manually inspect the ordinary and descriptor completed-projection flows to confirm no read path can invoke direct fill before projection drain assertions.

description: [Review finding] The DMS-1317 evidence matrix validation is too shallow to protect the evidence claims. `DocumentCacheEvidenceMatrixTests` verifies that each in-scope CDC-INV row appears, that referenced repository files exist, that external scope boundaries are labelled, and that each row contains a `src/dms` path. It does not verify that the named test methods or classes cited in `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md` actually exist in the referenced source files. A cited method such as a writer race, performance evidence, status endpoint, or completed-projection scenario could be renamed or removed while the matrix test still passes because the file remains present. Simplest responsible solution: extend `DocumentCacheEvidenceMatrixTests` so every cited test method/class name in `cdc-inv-evidence.md` must exist in the referenced source file.
acceptance-criteria: `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md` uses a consistent citation format that pairs each cited `.cs` evidence path with the concrete test method or class names being claimed from that file.

`DocumentCacheEvidenceMatrixTests` extracts every cited test method or class name from `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md` and asserts that the referenced source file contains that member name.
The existing evidence matrix checks for one row per in-scope CDC-INV contract, existing repository file paths, explicit E19/DMS-1318 boundaries, and concrete `src/dms` evidence remain in place.
The validation fails when a cited test method or class name in the matrix is misspelled, renamed, or removed from the referenced source file.
The validation remains a unit-level documentation/evidence guard and does not require PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Docker, or provider integration databases.
steps-to-verify: Temporarily change one cited method name in `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md`, confirm the matrix validation fails, and restore the correct citation.

description: [Review finding] The retryable-incomplete DocumentCache admin CLI tests use fixed 10.5-second sleeps after starting a command with a 10-second provider command timeout. PostgreSQL and SQL Server both wait for `Resetting`, then call `Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(10500))` before releasing the cache lock and awaiting process exit. This adds at least 21 seconds of unconditional wall-clock delay to the integration suite and keeps the tests timing-sensitive. Simplest responsible solution: replace the unconditional `Task.Delay(10500)` calls with a polling helper that waits until the CLI process exits with the expected retryable-incomplete result, bounded by the existing outer timeout.
acceptance-criteria: The PostgreSQL retryable-incomplete rebuild workflow no longer calls `Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(10500))` or any equivalent unconditional sleep to wait out the provider command timeout.
The SQL Server retryable-incomplete rebuild workflow no longer calls `Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(10500))` or any equivalent unconditional sleep to wait out the provider command timeout.

A shared helper keeps the blocking cache lock held after the lifecycle reaches `Resetting`, waits for the CLI process to exit with the expected retryable-incomplete result, and bounds that wait with the existing outer timeout.

The helper asserts the expected retryable-incomplete exit code and JSON result, including command `onlineCacheRebuild`, status `incompleteRetryable`, classification `providerCommandTimeout`, mutated `true`, and lifecycle `resetting`.

The tests release the blocking cache lock only after the retryable-incomplete process result has been captured, then reissue the same rebuild command and assert the workflow resumes to completed Tracking state with cache rows preserved and work rows drained.
No fixed sleep longer than a short polling interval remains in the retryable-incomplete CLI tests.
steps-to-verify: Manually inspect the PostgreSQL and SQL Server retryable-incomplete workflows to confirm process exit is awaited by the polling helper while the lock is still held.

description: [Plan step 1] Add DocumentCache representative qualification result models and artifact validation. The validator requires one and only one `threshold-results.json` row for every provider threshold defined in `DocumentCacheQualification.Thresholds`.
The validator requires every threshold row to include `provider`, `thresholdId`, `area`, `measurement`, `measuredValue`, `maximum`, `unit`, `passed`, `evidencePath`, and `reviewerNote`.
The validator rejects threshold rows whose `area`, `maximum`, or `unit` differs from the catalog entry.

The validator rejects absolute evidence paths, parent-directory traversal, missing evidence files, duplicate threshold rows, unknown threshold ids, and result directories missing required top-level artifacts.
The validator requires `durableBaselineCursorTicket` on failed interrupted restart-from-beginning rows and any failed interrupted-restart database-load, log-pressure, or queue-DML threshold row.

Unit tests cover successful validation, missing required artifacts, duplicate rows, missing rows, catalog mismatches, invalid paths, missing evidence paths, and required durable-baseline-cursor ticket failures.
steps-to-verify: Temporarily remove one required threshold row from a local sample artifact and confirm validation fails before restoring it.

`src/dms/tests/EdFi.DataManagementService.Performance.Harness/Runs/Given_Mssql_DocumentCacheRepresentativeRun.cs` exists and derives from the SQL Server API integration test base.

description: [Plan step 4] Reuse the existing 500k fixture loader for DocumentCache source cardinality. Simplest responsible solution: add DocumentCache-specific fixture setup that calls `PerfFixtureLoader` with `PerfFixtureKind.Primary500k` and records the database, fixture, source row count, cache row count, work row count, storage, and git identity evidence before benchmark phases start.

description: [Plan step 5] Implement the shared `DocumentCacheQualificationRunPipeline`. Simplest responsible solution: build one provider-agnostic orchestration pipeline that executes the required lifecycle, outage, status, write-overhead, contention, scrub, and final-count phases against the seeded 500k database.
acceptance-criteria: `DocumentCacheQualificationRunPipeline` exists in the performance harness and is called by both provider representative run fixtures.
The pipeline guards CI, tmpfs storage, dirty worktree state, fixture size, provider prerequisites, and connection identity before measurement begins.
The pipeline measures disabled canonical write samples before DocumentCache activation.
The pipeline runs offline activation or first baseline and records elapsed time until the target reaches `Tracking` and caught-up status.
The pipeline measures caught-up `Tracking` canonical write samples and computes the p95 write-overhead ratio versus `Disabled`.
The pipeline samples status and oldest-work latency while the work queue is empty, small, and large.
The pipeline runs online rebuild and records elapsed time for clear, reseed, drain, and return to `Tracking`.
The pipeline deterministically interrupts a `Rebuilding` command after partial progress is observed, reruns the replacement command, and records restart-from-beginning completion time.
The pipeline creates 50,000 distinct-document outage writes while projection is not draining, records distinct touched documents, records work-row growth, and computes the backlog growth ratio.
The pipeline drains the 50,000-row outage backlog and records elapsed drain time and final caught-up status.
The pipeline runs same-document enqueue/ack contention with 32 contenders and records p95 lock wait, retry count, and deadlock count.
The pipeline runs explicit scrub, records admission and elapsed time, and records final lifecycle, cache, work, and source counts.
Every pipeline phase writes a command transcript and a structured phase-metrics JSON artifact.
steps-to-verify: Run a reduced local smoke version of the pipeline and confirm every required phase writes a transcript and phase-metrics JSON file.
Inspect the interrupted rebuild smoke output and confirm the replacement command starts from `Rebuilding` state and records restart completion.

description: [Plan step 6] Implement PostgreSQL and SQL Server metric capture for DocumentCache representative qualification. Simplest responsible solution: add provider-specific capture services that snapshot WAL/log, plan/IO, status-query, maintenance, CPU, and IO evidence around the benchmark phases and write the required provider-metrics artifacts.
acceptance-criteria: PostgreSQL capture records WAL LSN before and after baseline, online rebuild, interrupted restart, and outage drain phases.
PostgreSQL capture computes WAL bytes per projected document with `pg_wal_lsn_diff`.
PostgreSQL capture writes `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON)` samples for projection, status, and oldest-work queries.
PostgreSQL capture records `pg_stat_user_tables` before the run, after the run, and after `VACUUM` for `dms.DocumentCache` and `dms.DocumentProjectionWork`.
PostgreSQL capture writes `provider-metrics/postgresql-wal-vacuum-bloat.md` and records the approved bloat-estimation output or the approved reason no bloat estimator was available.
SQL Server capture records `sys.dm_db_log_stats(DB_ID())` before and after baseline, online rebuild, interrupted restart, and outage drain phases.
SQL Server capture computes transaction log bytes per projected document.
SQL Server capture writes `SET STATISTICS IO` and actual plan XML samples for projection, status, and oldest-work queries.
SQL Server capture records `sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats` after the run and after cleanup or index maintenance for `dms.DocumentCache` and `dms.DocumentProjectionWork`.
SQL Server capture writes `provider-metrics/mssql-log-ghost-index.md` with ghost row ratio and fragmentation observations.
CPU and IO threshold evidence is read from a strict operator-supplied metrics file when the database provider does not expose reliable per-database CPU or IO directly.
The validator requires the CPU and IO metrics evidence file referenced by each CPU or IO threshold row.
steps-to-verify: Run provider metric capture against small local PostgreSQL and SQL Server fixtures and confirm both provider-metrics markdown files are written.
Remove the operator CPU metrics file from a local sample result and confirm validation fails.

description: [Plan step 7] Generate deterministic `threshold-results.json` from measured DocumentCache benchmark phases. Simplest responsible solution: map phase metrics and provider metric captures into one sorted JSON row per `DocumentCacheQualification.Thresholds` entry and validate the file before writing the final result directory.
acceptance-criteria: The representative benchmark writes `threshold-results.json` with one row per provider threshold id in `DocumentCacheQualification.Thresholds`.
Rows are sorted deterministically by provider and threshold id.
Rows use lower-camel property names and invariant-culture numeric values.

Rows include measured values and pass/fail results for baseline completion, online rebuild completion, interrupted restart-from-beginning completion, average database CPU, database IO, WAL or log growth, queue DML amplification, status/oldest-work p95 latency, canonical write-overhead p95 ratio, outage backlog growth ratio, outage drain completion, same-document enqueue/ack p95 lock wait, and provider maintenance ratio.
Every row's `maximum`, `unit`, `area`, and `measurement` come from the threshold catalog rather than duplicated literals.
Every row's `evidencePath` points to an existing phase transcript, phase metrics file, query-plan guard file, writer-contention evidence file, outage-drain evidence file, or provider-metrics file.
Failed interrupted restart-from-beginning rows and related failed interrupted-restart load/log/queue-DML rows include a non-empty `durableBaselineCursorTicket`.
The artifact writer validates the in-memory threshold rows, writes the JSON file, reloads the written file, and validates the file from disk.
steps-to-verify: Run a reduced local smoke benchmark and confirm `threshold-results.json` is sorted and reload-validates from disk.
Temporarily point a generated threshold row to a missing evidence path and confirm validation fails.

description: [Plan step 8] Create a separate performance engineer runbook from `plan.md` section 8. Simplest responsible solution: move the release-validation operator instructions into `reference/document-cache/representative-qualification-runbook.md` and link it from the DocumentCache qualification documentation.
acceptance-criteria: `reference/document-cache/representative-qualification-runbook.md` exists and is written as instructions for the performance engineer running the release-validation benchmark.

The runbook states that representative qualification must run only on dedicated PostgreSQL and SQL Server targets whose storage is not tmpfs and whose provider metrics can be captured for the full run window.

The runbook tells the engineer to record database host identity, image tag and digest or managed-service version, storage note, runner commit, subject commit, and dirty-path allowlist before starting.
The runbook includes the bounded guard and explicit writer evidence command from `plan.md` section 8.
The runbook includes the representative `-RunRepresentative -RunExplicitWriterEvidence` command from `plan.md` section 8.

The runbook lists the required result directory contents: `qualification-summary.md`, `threshold-results.json`, `query-plan-guards/`, `writer-contention-evidence/`, `outage-drain-evidence/`, both provider-metrics files, `command-transcripts/`, and `phase-metrics/`.
The runbook includes validation instructions for the produced result directory and the committed `reference/document-cache/qualification-results/<run-id>/` directory.
The runbook states the durable-baseline-cursor Jira ticket requirement for failed interrupted restart-from-beginning or related database-load, log-pressure, or queue-DML thresholds.
The runbook states that placeholder values, synthetic pass/fail rows, and non-representative local Docker measurements must not be committed as qualification evidence.
`reference/document-cache/performance-qualification.md` and `reference/document-cache/README.md` link to the new runbook.
steps-to-verify: Manually compare `reference/document-cache/representative-qualification-runbook.md` to `plan.md` section 8 and confirm all operator instructions were preserved.

description: [Representative evidence] Run the new benchmark and commit real PostgreSQL and SQL Server DocumentCache qualification artifacts. Simplest responsible solution: execute the performance engineer runbook, validate the produced artifacts, commit the validated result directory, and update evidence claims so DMS-1317 is not marked qualified without measured representative results.
acceptance-criteria: A validated result directory exists under `reference/document-cache/qualification-results/<run-id>/`.

The committed result directory contains `qualification-summary.md`, `threshold-results.json`, `query-plan-guards/`, `writer-contention-evidence/`, `outage-drain-evidence/`, `provider-metrics/postgresql-wal-vacuum-bloat.md`, `provider-metrics/mssql-log-ghost-index.md`, `command-transcripts/`, and `phase-metrics/`.
`threshold-results.json` contains measured PostgreSQL and SQL Server rows for every threshold in `DocumentCacheQualification.Thresholds`.

The measured rows cover baseline/rebuild completion time, interrupted restart-from-beginning completion time, database CPU/IO/log pressure, repeated queue DML or write amplification, status/oldest-work latency, canonical write overhead, queue growth and drain after outage, same-document enqueue/ack lock waits, and provider maintenance observations.
Every `evidencePath` referenced by `threshold-results.json` resolves inside the committed result directory.
The committed artifacts identify the representative workload as 500,000 canonical documents, 50,000 distinct-document outage writes, and 32 same-document enqueue/ack contenders.
When a required threshold fails, `threshold-results.json` records the durable-baseline-cursor Jira ticket and `qualification-summary.md` states that production qualification is not complete.

`reference/document-cache/performance-qualification.md`, `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md`, `reference/document-cache/README.md`, and `tasks.json` describe the committed evidence accurately and do not claim representative-scale qualification based only on bounded guards.

The original incomplete review-remediation task for representative-scale DocumentCache qualification can be marked complete only after the validated result directory and accurate documentation are committed.
steps-to-verify: Run: `jq 'length' reference/document-cache/qualification-results/<run-id>/threshold-results.json` and manually confirm the count matches `DocumentCacheQualification.Thresholds`.
Manually inspect `qualification-summary.md` and the provider-metrics files to confirm the run used valid non-tmpfs PostgreSQL and SQL Server performance targets.
